source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Persistent Uncorrectable Error in a Mirrored Region specific BIOS setup : • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — UEFI ARM Mirror = Enable — ARM Mirror Percentage = 10 — Patrol Scrub = Enable at End of Post — Mirror TAD0 = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — RAS Log Level = MID (BASIC_FLOW, FUNC_FLOW) • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > — Serial Debug Message Level > Normal 2. Halt the system and verify that mirroring is enabled by reading mode.mirror. >>> halt() >>> sv.sockets.compute0.uncore.memss.b2cmis.mode.mirror 3. Check the memory configuration to verify that the system is in mirror mode. Directory mode should be disabled and ECC should be enabled. Verify channel mode has P/P or ParMirr which indicates address range memory mirroring. >>> mc.dimminfoNoSPD() 4. Use mc.addTran() to print all valid TAD array entries to find the mirrored address range. >>> mc.addTran() 5. Use the following command to translate how a few address within the specified system address range map to its physical DIMM address. Take note of the memory controller ("mc") column. From this table, system address can be selected to test injecting errors into mirrored regions on different memory controllers. >>> ras.mem.sa2da_table(0x100000000, 0x100000400, 64) 6. Inject a persistent uncorrectable error to an address within the mirrored address region. >>> ei.utils.resetInjectorLockCheck() >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0msk=0x3, dev1msk=0x3) >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(0x100000300, oneInjection=False, errType="uce") 7. Verify the error was corrected. Check B2CMI_STATUS to verify a corrected error was logged. Alternatively, you can read the MCI_STATUS_SHADOW register. >>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.b2cmi1.mci_status_shadow >>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.b2cmi1.mci_status_shadow.show 8. Verify in the B2CMI_MISC register that the error was corrected during mirroring and mirror scrub was successful. Alternatively you can read the MCI_MISC_SHADOW register. >>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.b2cmi1.mci_misc_shadow >>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.b2cmi1.mci_misc_shadow.show() 9. A DDR channel failure should be logged and the failed channel should be identified for the mirror failover. Bits [1:0] correspond to channels 1 - 0. In this case, bit 0 of the ddr4chnlfailed is set. Meaning that channel 0 of memory controller 0 failed. >>> ei.utils.clearMemInjectors(socket=0) >>> go() >>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.b2cmi1.mirrorfailover.show() 10. FTrace Output. Verify an ELog record was generated indicated by extlog_mem_event. # cd /sys/kernel/debug/tracing # echo 1 > events/mce/mce_record/enable # echo 1 > events/ras/enable # cat trace_pipe

Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'mirror|uncorrected|uc'; echo __partial_mirror_Persistent_Uncorrectable_Error_in_a_Mirrored_Region; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

disposition_reason: Persistent corruption can be corrected from the mirror on first access yet make scrub back to the damaged channel fail, so the later channel-failure bit is the distinguishing result. Clearing the injector before go bounds further fault creation but does not erase the already written corruption. TAD/sa2da establishes that bit0 truly identifies the target MC0 channel0, while extlog establishes the error-reporting path. Repeating would confound both transition and recovery. test_case.test_name: Persistent Uncorrectable Error in a Mirrored Region — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify that a persistent UCE inside a 10% ARM mirrored region is handled and logged, then causes the mapped MC0 channel0 failover indication while the firmware-first extlog path remains observable.
required_package: CScripts version/hash/license and translated ARM/TAD/patrol paths
TAD/sa2da proof for0x100000300 and b2cmi1/MC0-ch0 mapping
Persistent masks, corrected/scrub and ddr4chnlfailed bit0 oracle
FTrace timing, serial/OOB and failed-channel recovery/restoration plan
test_case.test_command: Record baseline and literal ARM/TAD/patrol/RAS/debug settings; halt, verify mirror/ECC/P/P or ParMirr and map TAD/sa2da; reset injector lock, set both masks0x3 and inject persistent UCE at0x100000300; inspect b2cmi1 status/misc for correction and mirror scrub; clear injectors, go once, inspect b2cmi1 mirrorfailover for ddr4chnlfailed bit0 mapped to MC0 ch0; capture FTrace extlog_mem_event; recover failed channel and restore settings.
test_case.expected_result: Error is injected successfully. Error logs should match.
